Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Los Angeles/Oxnard CA 
355 AM PST Sat Nov 21 2026

.SYNOPSIS...20/1019 PM.

Dry and cooler weather is expected through Sunday morning. AThere
will be a chance of light rain Sunday and Sunday night. Light 
rain is possible again Tuesday night into Wednesday. Thanksgiving 
will be dry and warmer.

&&

.SHORT TERM (TDY-MON)...20/1151 PM.

Clear dry air has brought another chilly morning to the area today
with frost advisories in place across portions of the interior.
Despite a little ridge moving overhead, weak offshore flow and
copious sunshine, max temps will not rise much and will end up 4
to 8 degrees blo normal.

A cold upper low moving into the PACNW will push a trof and weak
front through the area on Sunday. The latest mdl runs have trended
a little stronger than the last few and it looks like most areas
will get some rain. SLO/SBA counties in the afternoon and VTA and
LA counties in the evening. While most areas will see rain no
area will see that much up to a quarter inch for the Central Coast
and maybe a tenth south of Pt Conception. The interior will not
even see a tenth. The southerly flow ahead of the front will bring
a degree maybe two of warming to the area.

A fast moving ridge will sweep over the area on Monday. Hgts will
bump up to 578 dam. Skies will be sunny and max temps will rise to
the mid 60s to lower 70s across the csts/vly. There will be a ~4
mb offshore push from the north in the morning and this will bring
some sub advisory gusts through and below the N/S oriented passes
and canyons.

.LONG TERM (TUE-FRI)...21/1204 AM.

The ridge will hold sway for most of Tuesday but a storm will be
approaching from the west. Skies will turn cloudier and cloudier
with time as the trof draws nearer. Any rain assoc the trof should
hold off until the evening. Even with the increased clouds max
temps will rise another 1 or 2 degrees and most cst/vly areas will
see max temps in the upper 60s and lower 70s. These temps are
mostly 2 to 4 degrees blo normal.

The trof will move over the area Tuesday night into early
afternoon Wednesday. It is a weak system and the only area with a
greater than 70 percent chc of rain is coastal SLO county. The
rest of the Central Coast only has a 50 percent chc of rain and
areas south of Pt Conception will only have a 20 to 30 percent
chc. Rainfall totals, if any, will be under a tenth of an inch
south of Pt Conception, a tenth to a quarter inch for the Central
Coast except north of Morro Bay where up to a half inch could
fall.

Thanksgiving and Black Friday will be sunny warmer and dry 
courtesy of an upper high to the SW with a ridge extending into 
Srn CA. Hgts will rise to 588 dam. There could be enough offshore 
flow for a moderate wind event. Look for about 6 degrees of 
warming on Thanksgiving and another 2 to 4 on Friday. Max temps 
Friday will be in the 70s across all csts/vly or 5 to 10 degrees 
over normals.

&&

.AVIATION...21/1049Z.

At 0822Z at KLAX, there was no marine layer nor an inversion.

Good confidence in TAFs except for KPRB where there is a 40
percent chc of LIFR conds. Gusty NE to E winds are possible for 
KOXR, KCMA, KSMO, KLAX, KVNY, and KBUR through 16Z and could 
create some light to moderate LLWS.

KLAX...High confidence in VFR TAF. A 7 kt east wind component is
possible through 15Z.

KBUR...High confidence in VFR TAF. Gusty N to E are possible
through 14Z with some light LLWS.

&&

.MARINE...21/1234 AM.

Good confidence that winds and seas will remain below small craft
advisory (SCA) levels through the weekend.

Two storms one later Sunday and overnight and another Wednesday.
These systems will bring the best chance of rain to the seas north
of Pt Conception. Post-frontal low-end SCA level NW-W winds will 
still be possible Wednesday/night south of Point Conception. A 
significant westerly swell (around 14-16 feet) is expected mid- 
week, with large, SCA level seas for the outer waters.

&&

.BEACHES...20/845 PM.

There is significant concern for moderate to major coastal
flooding Thanksgiving week. This is due to the combination
of kelvin wave/thermal expansion, Pergiean spring tides,
and a large long-period westerly swell (260-280 degrees).

================================================================

[For Central Coast, Ventura, and Los Angeles counties]:

A COASTAL FLOOD ADVISORY has been issued for Monday-Tuesday.

Potential impacts: shallow flooding of beach parking lots and 
unprotected roads, moderate beach erosion likely, isolated
damage to structures/building/roadways but could occur but is
unlikely. 

A COASTAL FLOOD WATCH has been issued for WEDNESDAY-THURSDAY. 

The swell will arrive during this period which will combine 
with the aforementioned factors. Still some uncertainty in 
regards to how timely these will combine, but regardless 
significant impacts seem probable. Timing of peak high tides are 
expected between 845-1000AM and predicted values are:
roughly 8.2-8.6 ft for LA/VTA and 7.9-8.2 ft for Central Coast.
The reasonable worst case scenario is 0.3-0.5 ft above these
values. A slight limiting factor that may prevent the worst case
scenario from materializes would be higher mean sea level pressure.

Potential impacts if upgraded to COASTAL FLOOD WARNING:

More extensive moderate coastal flooding reaching further inland,
moderate to high risk of damaging flooding of coastal roads and
structures, and significant beach erosion is likely.

Areas of greatest concern: Morro Bay, Pismo Beach, Oceano Dunes, 
& Cayucos/Avila/Pismo Piers. For LA: Santa Monica to Palo Verdes 
and Long Beach/Naples. For VTA, Faria to Silver Strand Beach 
including inside of harbors and Ventura Harbor. 

==================================================================

[For Santa Barbara South Coast & Catalina/Santa Barbara islands]:

A COASTAL FLOOD ADVISORY has been issued for Monday-Thursday.

Potential impacts: shallow flooding of beach parking lots and 
unprotected roads, moderate beach erosion likely, isolated
damage to structures/building/roadways but could occur but is
unlikely. 

Areas of greatest concern: Santa Barbara to Rincon and Jalama
Beach. 

Additional Information: Elevated to high surf is likely through
Thanksgiving week. Additional coastal hazards will likely be
needed for Friday.

==================================================================

In conclusion, this is a particularly concerning period for 
coastal flooding risks - Please read the "actions" section below. 

PRECAUTIONARY/PREPAREDNESS ACTIONS:

(1)Heed advice from local officials - Rely on their expertise
regarding preparedness, closures, and warnings. 

(2)Protect property - Take necessary actions such as setting up
sandbags or barriers in flood-prone areas.

(3)Avoid flood areas - Stay clear of rock jetties, and flooded
roads, walkways, and other normally dry places. 

(4)Monitor the forecast for latest information: weather.gov/LOX
and @nwslosangeles on social media. Be aware of when high tide
peaks in your area: tidesandcurrents.noaa.gov. Refer to LAXCFWLOX.
